parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal exposure, documented police/border targeting, facility ban, or trans-specific violence is documented; same-sex conduct was decriminalised and incitement/aggravating provisions exist on paper. Court protection for the LGBT organisation and broadly neutral, relatively tolerant attitudes are documented positives. Offsetting these are absent anti-discrimination protections, repeal of employment protection, no recorded prosecutions under the protective articles, dated and largely sexual-orientation-framed attitude evidence, family ostracisation/discrimination, and no documented traveller-facing information on entry, facilities, custody or care. Overall consequences of outing appear mainly social/service friction rather than detention, but protections are thin.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented entry refusal, marker-mismatch practice or screening for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: No documented traveller document acceptance; absence of domestic gender recognition is resident-facing only and not counted as visitor exposure.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown how a home-passport marker mismatch would be handled at checkpoints.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented trans-specific arrest, detention or prison-placement practice.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminal provision on gender identity documented; general election-related detentions contain no trans-specific content.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement if an unrelated arrest occurred is undocumented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom, hostel, ward or other facility exclusion for trans visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facilities exposure cannot be inferred from absent resident anti-discrimination law.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of care, medication seizure or ward misplacement for visitors.
care_services.protection: No documented care-access or anti-discrimination protection in health services.
care_services.interaction: Health discrimination is documented as a resident structural gap; visitor care access is undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing, morality policing or gender-expression offence documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Article 191 bans incitement/discrimination threats based on gender identity; Article 160 adds aggravation for homicide.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Paper protections exist but no prosecution under either article is recorded.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented traveller-family, care, education or facility rule for minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family ostracisation is documented for residents; no visitor/minor-specific consequence is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A 2015 activist statement said the community was not targeted by violence as in some regional countries, but faced discrimination; no later trans-specific violence assessment is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Dated surveys showed 85% opposed violence against LGBTQ people; current trans-specific prevalence is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social friction/discrimination may occur without documented police targeting or violence pattern.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory anti-discrimination protection in education, health, housing or employment; employment protection was repealed in 2024.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Highest court in 2017 struck down the moral-order registration clause and protected LGBT organisation status; incitement/aggravating provisions remain.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are narrow and untested in the dossier; unknowns on borders, custody, facilities and care remain unanswered questions, not documented exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having no documented traveller-facing criminal exposure and some formal protections, but lower because Meridia documents accepted markers, tribunal access and compensation, while this dossier has no documented working traveller remedy or entry practice.

Higher than a case with documented care refusal corrected by an ombudsperson, because no such refusal is documented here, but lower than a system with proven rapid health remedies since no care protection or enforcement is documented.

Materially lower because Norathia documents recognised passports, trained officers, legal aid and a successful tribunal remedy, whereas this dossier documents only paper incitement/aggravating provisions, no prosecutions, and no protections in key services.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime has no documented state-imposed universal exposure, organised targeting, imprisonment pathway or facility/custody rule for trans visitors. Decriminalisation, incitement and aggravating provisions, court protection for organising, and broadly neutral attitudes keep worst-case severity low. However, thin and dated evidence, no anti-discrimination law, repealed employment protection, untested protective articles, and undocumented entry, facilities, custody and care mean this is not a proven protective regime. The result is reduced but not low risk, with discrimination/friction the principal documented concern.
